text:
Egor Chinakhov arrived in Pittsburgh from Columbus with one standout trait: NHL EDGE puts his hardest shot in the top percentile of the league and his top speed in the 98th. Through 13 games as a Penguin he has three goals and five points, the latest a power-play goal with 29 seconds left in the first period of Saturday's win in Los Angeles.

His scoring rate, 1.52 points per 60, sits below his talent range (1.89 to 2.76), and his finishing is about even with his chances, so this isn't luck. The 5v5 picture is middling: Pittsburgh gets 48 percent of the expected goals with him on, five points worse than without him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking last season had him carrying the puck in on 54 percent of his entries and in the 83rd percentile for chances from the slot. Those habits should produce more than he's getting. Our range expects about 21 goals over a full season; he needs a steadier spot in the lineup to get there.
headline: Chinakhov has the tools; the points lag
